reasons.agent: The header build holds Developer, DeveloperOpus2 and QA; DeveloperOpus is free, and the query boundary is security work, so Opus.
reasons.checker: QA2 is free and has run the :8020 dedicated-Hub drives.
reasons.mode: Chained tasks with a drive at each end; a flow runs them in order.
reasons.stop: Stops when the tasks are done.

design:
Decisions with the operator, 2026-11-02:
- Current project only. A query never returns another project's rows, and the Hub enforces this rather than trusting each query to filter.
- Queries only: no stored tables or materialised datasets in this slice.
- Free text is queryable (agent output, trace tool arguments and results, model messages, command lines, message, queue and checkpoint text), and queries can match regular expressions, so a dashboard can count leaks or occurrences in conversations. Rejected: metrics and names only, which could not answer those questions.
- Never queryable: credentials (API keys, operator credentials, run tokens, the trace exporter's headers), this machine's paths (project directory, run workspaces, workspace fingerprints), and other projects' rows. Credentials have no chart value; paths and other projects matter once other users connect projects.
- The reference of what can be queried is generated by the Hub from the version that is running, so it always matches what a query can reach. Rejected: a hand-written schema description in the vault, which goes stale on the first migration and would cost a distillation on every upgrade. What the data means and its traps go in a vault note that agents read and add to.
- Charts are a fixed set of kinds the app draws in its own colours, type and light and dark themes. Rejected: agent-written visual code.
- A dashboard runs its queries when opened and when Refresh is pressed; it does not refresh on its own while open.
- A Hub upgrade that breaks a query is surfaced on the panel, not prevented.

Hazard (Tier 2): storing dashboards adds a table, so the operator's :8000 Hub runs a migration on its real database at its next restart after this lands on master. The migration only creates new tables and changes no existing one; rollback is the migration's downgrade dropping them, which loses only saved dashboards.

Status 2026-11-02: paused by the operator after the requirements; the tasks are not written yet and wait on the open questions.

checked: Live :8000 database read with mode=ro on 2026-11-02: 61 tables, 56 carry project_id; credential-bearing api_keys, operator_credentials, runs.capability_token_hash, trace_settings.otlp_headers; paths in projects.working_directory, runs.workspace_dir, workspace_fingerprints
Free-text columns scanned for real-length aw_live_ and Anthropic keys: none found
trace_spans holds 136,139 project-scoped spans with name, operation, status, start/end times and attributes
No charting library in hub/ui/package.json; chapter_versions not removed on project delete was a past defect (task-85a6c6d51cd8), hence ac-project-delete
limits: The hand-written reference queries for the three examples are not written yet; the acceptance-drive task writes them
The 10-second and 10,000-row limits are proposed numbers, not measured

open_questions.question: May a table panel show matched free text in full (for example the leaked value itself), or must panels over text show counts and masked excerpts only? Assumed for now: it shows what the query returns, since the screen is the operator's own machine.
Is the Dashboards screen and chart look designed first in a mock with the operator (as the spec header was), or left to the builder held only to the app's colours and type? Recommended: a mock first.
Are 10 seconds per query and 10,000 rows per result the right limits? Proposed, not measured; the traces hold about 136,000 spans.

Tasks are not written yet. Planned: acceptance drive with hand-written reference queries (fails on today's code first); query service and its boundary; dashboard store and agent tools; Dashboards screen and charts; ship. Builder DeveloperOpus, checker QA2.

problem: Questions about how the project is going — how much each spec cost, how often QA sends each model's work back, which kinds of task take longest, how many times something appears in the conversations — have no screen, although the Hub records everything needed to answer them. Today an answer is a one-off query an agent runs by hand, and it is lost with the conversation. This slice proves the loop the roadmap rests on: ask, get a dashboard with correct numbers in the app's look, reopen it later, and see it current.

requirements.rationale: An agent that cannot see what its query returns saves wrong numbers with confidence.
requirements.statement: Any agent can run a read-only query over the current project's data and receive its columns and rows, so it can check a query's result before it saves a dashboard.

requirements.rationale: One database holds every project on the Hub; the roadmap is heading towards other users' projects.
requirements.statement: A query never returns a row belonging to another project, whatever the query text says, including queries that omit a project filter, join tables, or read the list of projects.

A query cannot read credentials (API keys, operator credentials, run tokens, the trace exporter's headers) or this machine's paths (the project directory, run workspaces, workspace fingerprints); a query naming them is refused with a message saying what is not queryable.
A query cannot change any data: an insert, update, delete, schema change or attach is refused and the data is unchanged.

requirements.rationale: The operator wants to count leaks and occurrences of things in the conversations.
requirements.statement: Free-text data is queryable — agent output, the traces' tool arguments and results, model messages and command lines, and message, queue and checkpoint text — and a query can match a regular expression against any text column.

requirements.rationale: The Hub has a history of freezing when one piece of work holds it; a dashboard must not be the next one.
requirements.statement: A query that runs longer than 10 seconds is stopped and answers an error saying so; a result over 10,000 rows is cut to 10,000 and says it was cut; and running queries does not hold up the Hub's other work.

requirements.rationale: A hand-written description goes stale on the first migration.
requirements.statement: The Hub provides agents a reference of everything a query can reach — each table and column, its type and a short meaning — generated from the running version, and nothing in it is refused when queried.

The project's vault holds a note on what the data means and its traps, which the agent tools point agents to and which agents add to, seeded with the known traps (a send-back rejects every piece of evidence from that commit; cost per spec counts its tasks' building and reviewing runs).

An agent can save a dashboard to the current project with a name, a description of the question it answers, and panels, each with a title, a query and a chart kind; the dashboard records which agent made it and when, and survives a Hub restart.
A panel's chart kind is one of a fixed set — single number, table, bar, stacked bar and line — and every kind is drawn in the app's colours and type, readable in both light and dark themes.

The project has a Dashboards screen, reachable from the app's navigation, listing its dashboards with name, author and date; opening one runs all its queries and draws them, a Refresh button runs them again, and the dashboard shows when its data was last fetched. The operator can delete a dashboard there.

A panel whose query fails shows the error on that panel, and a panel whose result cannot be drawn as its chart kind (for example a line with no numeric column) shows a warning saying why; the other panels still draw.
Deleting a project removes its dashboards.

in_scope: Agent tools to read the query reference, run a read-only query and see its rows, and save, list and read dashboards
A Dashboards screen per project: list, open, refresh, delete
Panels: a title, a query and a chart kind from a fixed set, drawn in the app's style
Errors and warnings shown per panel
A vault note for what the data means, seeded with the gotchas already known
non_goals: Changing a saved dashboard by asking (slice change-by-asking); in this slice an agent saves a new dashboard or replaces one whole
Stored tables, materialised or reusable named datasets
Queries across projects, or any write to project data
Agent-written chart code or styles outside the app's look
Refreshing on a timer or as runs finish
Keeping saved queries working across Hub upgrades

summary: Any agent, asked in a conversation, writes queries over the current project's data (traces and free text included), checks their results, and saves a dashboard of panels drawn in the app's own chart kinds and colours. The project gets a Dashboards screen that lists them; opening one runs its queries, a Refresh button runs them again, and a panel whose query fails shows the error while the rest draws. The Hub publishes a reference of what can be queried, generated from the running version, and a vault note holds what agents learn about what the data means.
title: Ask any agent for a dashboard and get one that stays
